name: cx-sequence~p1
task: First find the key and then pick it up. After that, open the locked door, enter the room, and then pick up the ball.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands a sequence of steps (pick up the key, open the door, enter the room, pick up the ball). Only the final step has a hard Existence clause; the intermediate commanded steps (has_matching_key, target_door_open, target_room_entered) lack hard Existence clauses. According to the guidelines, each commanded step that is not the last of a hard precedence chain must have its own hard Existence. Add hard Existence(has_matching_key), hard Existence(target_door_open), and hard Existence(target_room_entered) (the existing Precedence clauses already enforce the ordering).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Existence clauses for key_found, has_matching_key, target_door_open, and target_room_entered are redundant. The precedence chain (key_found -> has_matching_key -> target_door_open -> target_room_entered -> target_picked_up) together with the hard Existence(target_picked_up) already forces all earlier events, so these Existence clauses repeat what is already required. Remove the redundant Existence(key_found), Existence(has_matching_key), Existence(target_door_open), and Existence(target_room_entered); keep the hard Precedence clauses and a single hard Existence(target_picked_up).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Existence clauses for key_found (R1), has_matching_key (R3), target_door_open (R5), and target_room_entered (R7) are redundant. The task only requires the ordered sequence of events and a final goal (target_picked_up). The precedence rules together with the environment constraints already guarantee those intermediate propositions when the later ones occur, so the explicit Existence clauses repeat what the other hard rules enforce. Remove these four Existence clauses and keep the precedence chain plus the final hard Existence(target_picked_up).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The clauses include hard Existence(key_found), Existence(has_matching_key), Existence(target_door_open), and Existence(target_room_entered). In the task, these events are only required as intermediate steps before the final goal. The ordering is already captured by the hard Precedence chain (key_found -> has_matching_key -> target_door_open -> target_room_entered -> target_picked_up) together with a hard Existence(target_picked_up). The Existence clauses for the earlier steps are redundant—they are implied by the final Existence plus the Precedence constraints and therefore add an unnecessary requirement. Remove the redundant hard Existence clauses for key_found, has_matching_key, target_door_open, and target_room_entered, keeping only the hard Existence(target_picked_up) and the five hard Precedence clauses.

The key must be found before it is picked up

The locked door must be opened before the target room is entered
The target room must be entered before the target ball is picked up
